title: Simulated DOM Event Pipeline with Propagation Control
subtopicTitle: DOM Event Flow: Capturing, Bubbling & Delegation
concept: Event Phases (Capture -> Target -> Bubble) and Immediate Stop
problemStatement: Implement `dispatchTreeEvent(treeRoot, targetNode, eventName)` that simulates full DOM event flow: executes capture listeners down from root, target listeners on target, then bubble listeners back up to root. Supports `event.stopPropagation()` and `event.stopImmediatePropagation()`.
interviewTrap: Many engineers do not know the exact order: capture flows strictly root -> target parent, while bubbling flows target parent -> root.

testCases.name: Executes capture then bubble in correct sequence
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [() => {}], bubble: [() => {}] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [() => {}] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

testCases.name: stopPropagation prevents bubbling to parent
testCases.input: child stops propagation during target phase
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [() => {}], bubble: [() => {}] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [e => e.stopPropagation()] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

testCases.name: Capture phase stops immediately when stopped at root
testCases.input: root stops propagation during capture phase
testCases.testFn: const root = { id: 'root', _listeners: { click: { capture: [e => e.stopPropagation()] } } }; const child = { id: 'child', parentNode: root, _listeners: { click: { bubble: [() => {}] } } }; return dispatchTreeEvent(root, child, 'click');

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Events travel down from `window` through the DOM tree (Capturing Phase) until they reach the target (Target Phase), then bubble back up to `window` (Bubbling Phase). Event delegation attaches a single listener to a common ancestor, querying `event.target.closest()`.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Event Phases (Capture -> Target -> Bubble) and Immediate Stop.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
